reference_rows_mismatch: Reference data has 2686 (matlab/openseespy) or 3500 (reference/cui) rows vs. 1900 input rows. Peak values match well, indicating peaks occur within the 19s input duration.

openseespy_vs_matlab.verdict: PASS - perfect agreement after Rayleigh damping fix

yielding_behavior.note: No yielding observed in any story. All three stories remained elastic throughout the 0.40g Northridge excitation. This is consistent with the yield displacements of 0.005m for all stories vs maximum interstory drifts well below this threshold.

root_cause_and_fix.bug: This OpenSeesPy version's rayleigh() command does not apply stiffness-proportional damping (beta_k*K) to twoNodeLink elements with uniaxial materials. Only mass-proportional Rayleigh (alpha_m*M) was active.
root_cause_and_fix.diagnostic_evidence: 1-DOF test: C_eff = 1.0 (alpha*m only) vs expected C_eff = 2.0 (alpha*m + beta*k). All three stiffness-proportional variants (current tangent, initial, committed) produce C_eff = 0.
root_cause_and_fix.fix: Stiffness-proportional Rayleigh damping replaced with Viscous uniaxialMaterial elements (alpha=1.0) placed parallel to each spring: C_visc_i = beta_k * k_i. Isolation dashpot combined: C_iso_vis = beta_k*keq + c_iso. Mass-proportional Rayleigh retained via ops.rayleigh(alpha_m, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0).

consistency_thresholds.reasoning: For nonlinear seismic analysis, peak response agreement within 1% across different software implementations indicates consistent modeling. The system does not yield, so dynamics are effectively linear.

final_verdict: PASS - MATLAB, OpenSeesPy, and ABAQUS show essentially perfect agreement (all peak errors < 0.005%). Bug in OpenSeesPy stiffness-proportional Rayleigh damping identified and corrected via equivalent Viscous element formulation. All three software paths produce auditable, numerically consistent results.
